CLINICAL STUDY REPORT — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Moderna, Inc. | mRNA-1273.222-P301

Study ID: mRNA-1273.222-P301
Study Name: Bivalent Booster Study
Phase: Phase 3
Title: Bivalent Omicron BA.4/BA.5 Booster
Study Period: 10 April 2024 to 02 November 2025
Number of Subjects: 511
Study Sites: 194 sites across United States
IND Number: IND-6295-90
Report Date: 16 October 2026
Medical Monitor: Katelyn Mejia, MD, PhD
1. Synopsis
This Clinical Study Report summarizes the results of Bivalent Booster Study (mRNA-1273.222-P301), a Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy of mRNA-1273 in 511 participants. The study was conducted in accordance with ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice guidelines and applicable regulatory requirements.
2. Study Design
Design: Randomized, Observer-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled
Randomization Ratio: 1:1 (Vaccine:Placebo)
Dosing Schedule: Two doses (Day 1 and Day 29)
Dose: 100 mcg (0.5 mL IM injection)
Follow-up Period: 24 months post-dose 2

4. Safety Summary
The vaccine demonstrated an acceptable safety profile. The most common solicited adverse events were injection site pain (94%), fatigue (66%), headache (66%), and myalgia (57%). The majority of adverse events were mild to moderate and resolved within 1-3 days. Serious adverse events (SAEs) occurred in 1.0% of vaccine recipients vs 1.2% of placebo recipients. No vaccine-related SAEs led to death.
5. Immunogenicity Summary
mRNA-1273 induced robust and durable neutralizing antibody responses. Geometric mean titers (GMTs) at Day 57 were 916 (95% CI: 794 – 2093). Seroconversion rates were 98.2% at 28 days post-dose 2. T-cell responses (CD4+ and CD8+) were also observed in a subset analysis.
6. Conclusions
mRNA-1273 demonstrated 93.6% efficacy against COVID-19 and an acceptable safety profile consistent with other approved vaccines. These results support the benefit-risk assessment for regulatory approval in the indicated population.
